learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of mathematical principles and understanding of the role of mathematical sciences as a tool for analysis and problem-solving and models underlying industrial engineering and in particular mechanical engineering. Knowledge of the principles of computer science and the algorithmic and numerical approach to problems.
Knowledge of information technologies, their role in supporting design. Understanding the organization of information in databases and computer-aided design to support processes.

Ability to apply mathematical methods – with particular reference to methods related to differential and integral calculus, geometry, linear algebra, numerical calculus, and probability and statistics – to model, analyze, and solve engineering problems, also with the aid of computer tools.
Ability to analyze data and information using known methods and tools, interpret results, and draw consistent conclusions, also with the support of provided indications.
Ability to compare different options or solutions to an engineering problem and contribute to motivated technical choices, referring to technical standards and standard industry procedures.
Ability to work in a group collaboratively and coordinately, understanding the context of the engineering problem and recognizing the main interdisciplinary implications of the application area.

Ability to organize one's work respecting assigned commitments and deadlines, managing available time and resources, realistically evaluating one's abilities, and contributing to activity prioritization.
Ability to recognize one's knowledge limits and the need to acquire new skills, identifying adequate information sources and guided learning opportunities.
Ability to present problems, solutions, analyses, and results clearly and structured through written reports and oral presentations, according to standard methods and formats.
Ability to represent and graphically communicate data, results, and technical solutions, by drafting diagrams, graphs, and tables, using consolidated tools and conventions.

Ability to find and consult bibliographic sources and technical documentation through the main available resources (libraries, databases, manuals, and digital sources), selecting relevant information with the support of provided indications.

Knowledge of mathematical principles and understanding of the role of mathematical sciences as a tool for analysis and problem-solving and models underlying industrial engineering and in particular management engineering. Knowledge of linear and non-linear optimization models and understanding of their field of application. Knowledge of the fundamental principles of inferential statistics and statistical methods applicable to the industrial context. Knowledge of the principles of computer science and the algorithmic approach to problems.

Understanding of the broader multidisciplinary context of engineering. They are oriented towards problem-solving, which starts from the problem to trace back to causes and possible measures to address them, typically multidisciplinary.

Ability to solve problems in mathematics, geometry, probabilistic and sampling estimation, linear algebra and linear programming, finding stationary points and optima, developing algorithms on computer tools.

Ability to choose and apply appropriate analytical and modeling methods, and in particular mathematical analysis, operational research modeling or practical experimentation supported by statistical methods; in particular, these abilities are developed in experimental laboratory learning and in the creation of design works.

Ability to apply one's knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve industrial and specifically management engineering problems, defining specifications, technical constraints, but also social, health and safety, environmental and commercial, and to solve them using consolidated methods; each taught discipline provides, even if not organized in laboratories, moments of exercise and practical application of the methods learned. The characterizing disciplines must develop the multidisciplinary skills required of the engineer.
Ability to choose and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods for the production of goods and services.
Ability to combine theory and practice to solve multidisciplinary engineering problems, taking into account non-technical constraints as well.

syllabus_topics: Program execution and environments: notebooks, IDE, console
Mutable and immutable types in Python
While and for loops in Python
Data structures and elementary algorithms: Lists, Dictionaries, Sets
Binary search trees: Recursive traversal, Search, Ordered insertion
Introduction to data analysis, reading and writing tabular files, graphs
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written and an oral part. Students must be able to solve problems using algorithms with the aid of computer tools and demonstrate knowledge of data structures (strings, arrays, matrices, lists, dictionaries) and their implementation in Python. The grading scale ranges from 'Insufficient' (due to serious conceptual errors or lack of understanding) to '29-30 e Lode' (for complete, in-depth knowledge and critical thinking). 'Lode' is awarded for particularly brilliant and original work.
